text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD_INC-5123 — sustained CUDA OOMs on gpu-pool (cluster-chi-rt-2). auto-escalation in 5m if not acked

pagerduty: Alert details: service=redwood-inference-gpu, symptom=CUDA_ALLOC_FAILURE spike, recent rate=23/min, impacted-tenants=2 (high priority)

jordan: acked. i'm taking first touch. can someone pull recent logs and host / pod IDs?

maya: pulling from monitoring — looks like several pods on node chi-gpu-07 hit OOM around 12:14UTC. grabbing kube events now.

maya: kube events snippet:
```
$ kubectl get events -n inference --field-selector involvedObject.name=llm-worker-7b-0
LAST SEEN   TYPE     REASON             OBJECT                                  MESSAGE
1m          Warning  OOMKilled          pod/llm-worker-7b-0                      container "model" was OOMKilled
1m          Warning  BackoffRestart     pod/llm-worker-7b-0                      Back-off 5m0s restarting failed container
```

maya: and recent container logs show repeated allocation failures: 
```
[2026-03-14T12:14:21Z] ERROR runtime.cpp:452 CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 512MB
[2026-03-14T12:14:22Z] WARN  kvcache.cpp:89 KV cache miss spike, falling back to full recompute
[2026-03-14T12:14:23Z] ERROR scheduler.cpp:278 failed to reserve GPU memory: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```

lin: looks like model prompting pattern changed — longer prefixes from a customer causing seq len spike. are we using dynamic batching? which quant/profile?

jordan: model is 7B-q4f but running with prefix caching enabled; scheduler should drop to single-request mode but something prevented reclaim. maybe an unbounded KV cache growth.

dave: tagging ops-runbook-bot for standard GPU OOM mitigation steps :eyes: 

ops-runbook-bot: ACTIONS recommended:
1) cordon + drain node if multi-pod impact (kubectl cordon/drain chi-gpu-07)
2) restart afflicted pods with reduced max_seq / disable prefix cache via env override MODEL_PREFIX_CACHE=0
3) if canary/replica, scale up warm nodes to absorb traffic
4) collect nvidia-smi, dmesg, and coredump (if any)
5) notify affected customers and enable temporary rate-limit per-tenant

maya: nvidia-smi snapshot from chi-gpu-07:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 12.2     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100-40GB   Off           | 00000000:3B:00.0 Off | 0                    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 0  13228MiB / 40960MiB |   32% Default |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

lin: memory usage spikes correlate with specific request IDs? maya can you grep logs for request ids and tokens-per-request?

maya: yes — found 3 requests with token_count ~ 64k in the last 10m (customer: acme-ads). sample request id: req-8a3f2c. That explains the allocs.

jordan: ok mitigation plan:
- temporary rate-limit acme-ads to 5 concurrent requests and cap prompt length at 8k tokens via routing policy
- restart the 3 OOM pods with MODEL_PREFIX_CACHE=0 and MAX_SEQ=8192
- cordon chi-gpu-07 and move remaining pods off (drain)

lin: i can apply the routing policy change and set rate-limits. handing off node drain to dave if that's ok?

dave: on it. will drain chi-gpu-07 now (evicting non-critical pods), leaving reserved capacity untouched.

dave: drain command:
```
kubectl cordon chi-gpu-07 && kubectl drain chi-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force -n inference
```

dave: evictions kicked off, two pods failed immediate grace due to large volumes; opened ticket to restart those after env change.

jordan: maya — can you push env override for the affected deployment? small snippet: 
```yaml
env:
  - name: MODEL_PREFIX_CACHE
    value: "0"
  - name: MAX_SEQ
    value: "8192"
```

maya: pushed config and triggered rollout with canary=1. logs show new pod stabilizing.

pagerduty: PD_INC-5123 acknowledged by jordan. Escalation suspended.

lin: i've applied tenant-level limit for acme-ads and added a temporary pre-filter to reject >8k token prompts with a 429 and guidance.

acme-ads-notify-bot: Draft notice prepared: "We observed unusually long prompts from your integration causing GPU memory pressure; we've temporarily limited request size and concurrency while we stabilize. We'll follow up with recommended client-side limits."

jordan: good. i'll ping CS to send the notice and create a follow-up with product for a durable policy on prompt size enforcement.

dave: drain completed. chi-gpu-07 cordoned. overall cluster GPU utilization back to normal on other nodes.

maya: monitoring shows OOM events dropped to zero after rollout/restart and tenant rate-limit change. keeping watch for 30m.

jordan: switching to monitoring mode. leaving handoff notes: impacted pods: llm-worker-7b-{0,1,3}, node chi-gpu-07, root cause likely customer-generated long context. mitigation: restart with cache off, tenant rate-limit, node drained, customer notified.

lin: i'll own the long-term follow-up (postmortem + durable prompt-length guardrails). tagging dave for infra follow-up on eviction behavior. :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks team. closing PD when stable. will update thread in 30m. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Note: If any further OOMs occur, PagerDuty will re-escalate. Keep channel updated."
